verdict.rationale: Greptile documents several programmatic surfaces that mirror dashboard functions. `greptile onboard` performs "the same setup the dashboard does". The MCP server lets users fetch comments, apply fixes and manage patterns "instead of switching to GitHub or the Greptile dashboard". `greptile.json` overrides dashboard settings, and the CLI accepts an API key for CI use. However, no public REST/OpenAPI spec was found (probes returned 404), and some settings, such as Default Coding Agents, are documented only as dashboard actions. Missing for 10: a documented general-purpose API with an OpenAPI spec, an explicit claim of full UI/API parity, programmatic coverage of org settings such as Default Coding Agents, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: `greptile onboard` creates your organization, connects GitHub or GitLab, enables repositories, and imports your existing AI rules files — the same setup the dashboard does.
Instead of switching to GitHub or the Greptile dashboard, you can fetch comments, apply fixes, and manage coding patterns from your editor.
Settings are read from the source branch of the PR and override dashboard settings.
For CI or self-hosted deployments, use an API key: export GREPTILE_API_KEY=... greptile review
